member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type0FunctionElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

This class represents the calibrated gray color space. Calibrated color spaces specify values which are device independent and more akin to the way we perceive colors. The result is that, within the limits of an output device, calibrated colors will appear the same even when displayed on different devices.
This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 63, page 145.

summary.para: This property represents the type of color space.
It is a property of type ColorSpaceType.

This class represents a device color space. Device color spaces represent generic grayscale, RGB or CMYK outputs. These types of color spaces represent physical quanties. So a grayscale value represents a literal amount of black ink on paper. Because no color profile information is contained, device colors may vary between different outputs. For example 50% copverage of one type of black ink on gloss paper may look different to 50% of another black ink on matte.
This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Section 8.6.4: 62, page 124.

summary.para: This class represents a DeviceN or multi-separation color space. A DeviceN color space represents a set of custom colors. Most typically these are spot colors used in printing. For example the conventional color space for printing is CMYK and for that you can use the DeviceCMYK color space. However processes like Hexachrome added orange and green inks to better represent a wider range of colors. Using a DeviceN color space you can specify a CMYKOG color space which will print correctly on a Hexachrome printer. The DeviceN color space includes a conversion function so that it will also provide a good representation on screen and on normal CMYK printers.
This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Section: 8.6.6.5, page 159.

summary.para: This property represents the names of the colors within the DeviceN color space.

The names are arbitrary values such as "Seabreeze" which are intended for human readability. These may include the special value "None" which indicates no color, but may not include the special value "All". Each name should be unique, with the exception of the special value "None" which may be repeated.

For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 160.

This property represents the tint transform function.

The function is used to map color values in the DeviceN color space into color values in the EntryAlternateColorSpace color space. The function should be called with the tint value and should return a number of components in the alternate color space.

For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 160.
This property represents addition attributes specific to this color space.

This class represents an ICC calibrated color space. Calibrated color spaces specify values which are device independent and more akin to the way we perceive colors. The result is that, within the limits of an output device, calibrated colors will appear the same even when displayed on different devices. The International Color Consortium (ICC) defines standards for cross-platform, standardized, calibrated color spaces. ICC color spaces encompass a wide range of color spaces with characteristics contained in a color profile data package.
This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 66, page 149.

summary.para: Create a new AlternateImageElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.AlternateImageElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the calgray colour space dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 63, page 145.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 62, page 183.

member.summary:
Represents the "Subtype" entry of the devicen colour space attributes dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.6 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "DeviceN" if no value has been provided.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
DeviceN
NChannel
For definitive details see:

The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 70, page 203.

It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.

member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the devicen process dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 72, page 163.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 71, page 205.

summary.para: Create a new GraphicsStateParameterElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.GraphicsStateParameterElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the icc profile stream dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 66, page 149.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 65, page 188.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because it is also a StreamElement and these are always indirect objects.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the lab colour space dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 65, page 148.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 64, page 186.

member.summary: Create an empty LabColorSpaceAttributesElement. The Element created by this default constructor is empty - it has no Atom within it. Before use an atom must be Assigned or Created. In practice it is easiest to do this using one of the other constructors.

An IndirectObject. This can be any IndirectObject from the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with the Atom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.LabColorSpaceAttributesElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new LabColorSpaceAttributesElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.LabColorSpaceAttributesElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OptionalContentConfigElement.EntryIntent
member.summary:
Represents the "Intent" entry of the optional content configuration dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF name objects. The PDF specification states that items in this array assume a value of "View" if no value has been provided.
Items in this array may take one of the following valid values:
View
Design
All
If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
The specification defines this as exensible which means that it may contain entries in addition to those defined in the specification. In fact almost all objects are extensible but the fact that it is explicitly mentioned, implies that extra entries should be regarded as normal rather than exceptional. For further details see The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: Annex E, page 673..
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 101, page 229.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 99, page 282.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the optional content group dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 98, page 222.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 96, page 273.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because OptionalContentPropertiesElement.EntryOCGs requires it to be so.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OptionalContentGroupElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new OptionalContentGroupElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OptionalContentGroupElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the optional content usage dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 102, page 232.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 100, page 284.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OptionalContentUsageElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new OptionalContentUsageElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OptionalContentUsageElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Create a new OptionalContentUsagePrintElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OptionalContentUsagePrintElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the optional content usage user dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 102, page 232.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 100, page 284.

summary.para: Represents the "Name" entry of the optional content usage user dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 102, page 232.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the reference dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 97, page 221.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 95, page 272.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ReferenceElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.param: The Validation object which will receive validation results and progress.

summary.para: Represents the "Domain" entry of the type 1 shading dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains doubles, representing PDF numeric objects.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 79, page 185.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 78, page 230.

summary.para: Represents the "Matrix" entry of the type 1 shading dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains doubles, representing PDF numeric objects.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 79, page 185.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 78, page 230.

summary.para: Represents the "Function" entry of the type 1 shading dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains FunctionElements.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one FunctionElement may be represented as a single FunctionElement rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 79, page 185.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 78, page 230.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the type 2 pattern dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 76, page 181.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 75, page 225.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type2PatternElement.#ctor
member.summary: Create an empty Type2PatternElement. The Element created by this default constructor is empty - it has no Atom within it. Before use an atom must be Assigned or Created. In practice it is easiest to do this using one of the other constructors.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type2PatternElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)

summary.para: Create a Type2PatternElement wrapping an Atom. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns the Atom to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the Atom.

member.param: The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
An IndirectObject. This can be any IndirectObject from the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with the Atom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type2PatternElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)

summary.para: Create a Type2PatternElement wrapping an IndirectObject. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns the IndirectObject to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the IndirectObject.

member.param: The IndirectObject to be assigned to this Element.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type2PatternElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new Type2PatternElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.summary: Creates a deep copy of the current Element.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type4ShadingElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.param: The IndirectObject to be assigned to this Element.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type5ShadingElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new Type5ShadingElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type5ShadingElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "BitsPerCoordinate" entry of the type 5 shading dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an integer representing a PDF numeric object.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 83, page 193.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 82, page 240.

The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 82, page 240.

summary.para: Represents the "Decode" entry of the type 5 shading dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains doubles, representing PDF numeric objects.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 83, page 193.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 82, page 240.

summary.para: Represents the "Function" entry of the type 5 shading dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains FunctionElements.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one FunctionElement may be represented as a single FunctionElement rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 83, page 193.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 82, page 241.

summary.para: Represents the "VerticesPerRow" entry of the type 5 shading dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an integer representing a PDF numeric object.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 83, page 193.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 82, page 240.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the type 6 shading dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 84, page 196.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 83, page 244.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because it is also a StreamElement and these are always indirect objects.

summary.para: Create a new XObjectElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.XObjectElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Type" entry of the xobject object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. If provided, this item must always take the value "XObject".
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 201.

summary.para: Represents the "AF" entry of the xobject object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 2.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains FileSpecificationElements.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 201.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the encoding dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 114, page 263.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the font dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 254.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because GraphicsStateParameterElement.EntryFont requires it to be so.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FontElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new FontElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FontElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the halftone dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 308.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.HalftoneElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "HalftoneName" entry of the type 1 halftone dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 130, page 309.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 128, page 371.

summary.para: Represents the "Frequency" entry of the type 1 halftone dictionary object.

It contains a double representing a PDF numeric object.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 130, page 309.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 128, page 371.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type1HalftoneElement.EntrySpotFunction
member.summary:
Represents the "SpotFunction" entry of the type 1 halftone dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of two different types:
1) A string representing a PDF name object.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
SimpleDot
InvertedSimpleDot
DoubleDot
InvertedDoubleDot
CosineDot
Double
InvertedDouble
Line
LineX
LineY
Round
Ellipse
EllipseA
InvertedEllipseA
EllipseB
EllipseC
InvertedEllipseC
Square
Cross
Rhomboid
Diamond
2) A FunctionElement.
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 130, page 309.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 128, page 371.

summary.para: Represents the "AccurateScreens" entry of the type 1 halftone dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a bool representing a PDF boolean object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of false if no value has been provided.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 130, page 309.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 128, page 371.

summary.para: Represents the "TransferFunction" entry of the type 1 halftone dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of two different types:
1) A string representing a PDF name object. If provided, this item must always take the value "Identity".
2) A FunctionElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 130, page 310.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 128, page 371.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the type 5 halftone dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 134, page 315.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 132, page 377.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Type5HalftoneElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new Type5HalftoneElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.GroupAttributesElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "TR" entry of the soft-mask dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of two different types:

1) A string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "Identity" if no value has been provided. If provided, this item must always take the value "Identity".
2) A FunctionElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 144, page 347.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 142, page 416.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the action dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 193, page 414.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 196, page 502.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ActionElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new ActionElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ActionElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Next" entry of the action dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.2 specification.
It contains an array which contains ActionElements.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one ActionElement may be represented as a single ActionElement rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 193, page 414.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the appearance characteristics dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 189, page 409.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 192, page 496.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.AppearanceCharacteristicsElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new AppearanceCharacteristicsElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.AppearanceCharacteristicsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.BorderEffectElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new BorderEffectElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.BorderEffectElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.BorderEffectElement.EntryS
member.summary:
Represents the "S" entry of the border effect dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "S" if no value has been provided.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
S
C
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 167, page 387.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 169, page 470.

summary.para: Represents the "I" entry of the border effect dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.

It contains a double representing a PDF numeric object. It should have a minimum value of 0 and a maximum of 2. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of 0 if no value has been provided.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 167, page 387.

summary.para: Represents the "URLType" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CollectionColorsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the collection field dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 157, page 372.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 155, page 448.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 8.8, page 30.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CollectionFieldElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new CollectionFieldElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CollectionFieldElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.DocumentPartGoToActionElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new DocumentPartGoToActionElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

summary.para: Represents the "Dp" entry of the document part go-to action object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 2.0 specification.
It contains a DocumentPartElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 206, page 512.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the document security store dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 261, page 582.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because SignatureValidationRelatedInformationElement.EntryCRL and SignatureValidationRelatedInformationElement.EntryOCSP require it to be so.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.DocumentSecurityStoreElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

It contains a string representing a PDF name object. If provided, this item must always take the value "DSS".

summary.para: Represents the "F" entry of the embedded go-to action object.

It contains a FileSpecificationElement.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 201, page 420.

summary.para: Represents the "D" entry of the embedded go-to action object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of three different types:
1) A string representing a PDF name object.
2) A string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
3) A DestinationElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 201, page 420.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 204, page 510.

The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 204, page 510.
