para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 201, page 420.

It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 243, page 459.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 246, page 556.

summary.para: Represents the "Status" entry of the fdf dictionary object.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 243, page 459.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FDFElement.EntryEncoding
member.summary:
Represents the "Encoding" entry of the fdf dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.3 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "PDFDocEncoding" if no value has been provided.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
PDFDocEncoding
Shift
BigFive
GBK
UHC
utf
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 243, page 459.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the fdf field dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 246, page 461.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 249, page 559.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FDFFieldElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new FDFFieldElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FDFFieldElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "V" entry of the fdf field dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of five different types:
1) A string representing a PDF name object.
2) An array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
3) A Null.
4) A SignatureElement.
5) A StreamElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 246, page 461.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 249, page 559.

It contains a FileSpecificationElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 250, page 464.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 253, page 562.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the fdf page dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 248, page 463.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 251, page 561.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FDFPageElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new FDFPageElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FDFPageElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "V" entry of the field dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of five different types:
1) A string representing a PDF name object.
2) An array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
3) A Null.
4) A SignatureElement.
5) A StreamElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 220, page 433.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FixedPrintElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.FormFieldAdditionalActionsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.IconFitElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the line annotation. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 175, page 398.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 178, page 482.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because it inherits from MarkupAnnotationElement which is always an indirect object.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.LineAnnotationElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new LineAnnotationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.MeasureElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.NavigationNodeElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

Represents the "O" entry of the number format dictionary object.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the outline dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 152, page 368.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 150, page 442.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because CatalogElement.EntryOutlines and OutlineItemElement.EntryParent require it to be so.

An IndirectObject. This can be any IndirectObject from the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with the Atom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OutlineElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new OutlineElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OutlineElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Create a new PageObjectAdditionalActionsElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.PageObjectAdditionalActionsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ProjectedCoordinateSystemElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the requirement dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 264, page 484.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 274, page 603.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.RequirementElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the richmediaanimation dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 337, page 699.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.50c, page 81.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.RichMediaAnimationElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new RichMediaAnimationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.RichMediaAnimationElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the richmediacontent dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 341, page 704.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.51, page 86.

summary.para: Create a new RichMediaContentElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.RichMediaContentElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.SignatureElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new SignatureElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.SignatureElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Type" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. If provided, this item must always take the value "Sig".
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 467.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 565.

summary.para: Represents the "Filter" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object.

The specification defines this as exensible which means that it may contain entries in addition to those defined in the specification. In fact almost all objects are extensible but the fact that it is explicitly mentioned, implies that extra entries should be regarded as normal rather than exceptional. For further details see The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: Annex E, page 673..
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 467.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 565.

summary.para: Represents the "SubFilter" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.3 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object.

The specification defines this as exensible which means that it may contain entries in addition to those defined in the specification. In fact almost all objects are extensible but the fact that it is explicitly mentioned, implies that extra entries should be regarded as normal rather than exceptional. For further details see The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: Annex E, page 673..
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 467.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 565.

summary.para: Represents the "Contents" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 468.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 565.

summary.para: Represents the "Cert" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 468.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 566.

summary.para: Represents the "ByteRange" entry of the signature dictionary object.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 468.

summary.para: Represents the "Reference" entry of the signature dictionary object.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 468.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the signature field time stamp dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 234, page 447.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 237, page 542.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 262, page 584.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.TargetElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.TargetElement.EntryR
member.summary:
Represents the "R" entry of the target dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
P
C
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 202, page 420.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 205, page 510.

summary.para: Represents the "N" entry of the target dictionary object.
It is defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 202, page 420.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 205, page 510.

summary.para: Represents the "P" entry of the target dictionary object.
It is defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of two different types:
1) An integer representing a PDF numeric object.
2) A string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 202, page 420.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 205, page 510.

summary.para: Represents the "A" entry of the target dictionary object.
It is defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of two different types:
1) An integer representing a PDF numeric object.
2) A string representing a PDF string object.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 202, page 420.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 205, page 510.

summary.para: Represents the "T" entry of the target dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a TargetElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 202, page 420.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 205, page 510.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the text annotation. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 172, page 394.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 175, page 478.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.TextAnnotationElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new TextAnnotationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ThreadElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the transform parameters dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 470.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.TransformParametersElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new TransformParametersElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.TransformParametersElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.TransitionElement.EntryS
member.summary:
Represents the "S" entry of the transition dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "R" if no value has been provided.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
Split
Blinds
Box
Wipe
Dissolve
Glitter
R
Fly
Push
Cover
Uncover
Fade
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 162, page 378.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 164, page 459.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the viewer preferences dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 150, page 362.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 147, page 435.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 8.1, page 28.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ViewerPreferencesElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new ViewerPreferencesElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ViewerPreferencesElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ViewportElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new ViewportElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.ViewportElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Create a new D3DActivationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.D3DActivationElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the 3D angular dimension measurement. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 329, page 689.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.39d, page 68.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.D3DBackgroundElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.D3DCrossSectionElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the 3D reference dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 303, page 519.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 314, page 648.

member.summary: Create an empty D3DReferenceElement. The Element created by this default constructor is empty - it has no Atom within it. Before use an atom must be Assigned or Created. In practice it is easiest to do this using one of the other constructors.

summary.para: Create a D3DReferenceElement wrapping an Atom. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns the Atom to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the Atom.

member.param: The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
An IndirectObject. This can be any IndirectObject from the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with the Atom.

summary.para: Create a D3DReferenceElement wrapping an IndirectObject. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns the IndirectObject to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the IndirectObject.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.D3DReferenceElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new D3DReferenceElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.D3DReferenceElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the 3D view dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 304, page 521.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 344, page 707.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.39, page 57.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.51f, page 93.
