member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.D3DViewElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new D3DViewElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.D3DViewElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

It contains an integer representing a PDF numeric object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of 4 if no value has been provided.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 284, page 500.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 295, page 626.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the media clip data dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 274, page 492.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 285, page 617.

summary.para: Create a new MediaClipDataElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.MediaClipDataMhBeElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.MediaClipSectionMhBeElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.MediaPermissionsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.MediaPlayParametersElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.

member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the minimum bit depth dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

summary.para: Represents the "Start" entry of the movie activation dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of three different types:
1) An integer representing a PDF numeric object. It should have a minimum value of 0.
2) A string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
3) An array which contains Elements.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 296, page 508.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 307, page 635.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.MovieElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new MovieElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.MovieElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the projection dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 305, page 524.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 316, page 655.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the rendition mh/be dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

summary.para: Create a new RenditionMhBeElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.RenditionMhBeElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Create a new SoundObjectStreamElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.SoundObjectStreamElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the box style dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 361, page 631.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 397, page 811.

summary.para: Create a new BoxStyleElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.BoxStyleElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.MetadataStreamElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the namespace dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 356, page 725.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because AttributeObjectElement.EntryNS, NamespaceElement.EntryRoleMapNS and StructureElementElement.EntryNS require it to be so.

An IndirectObject. This can be any IndirectObject from the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with the Atom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OutputIntentElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new OutputIntentElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.OutputIntentElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Type" entry of the output intent dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. If provided, this item must always take the value "OutputIntent".
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 365, page 633.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 401, page 814.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the destoutputprofileref dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 402, page 817.

For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the source information dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 355, page 623.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 391, page 803.

summary.para: Create a new SourceInformationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.StandardLayoutAttributesElement.EntryBorderStyle
member.summary:
Represents the "BorderStyle" entry of the standard layout attributes object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.5 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF name objects. The PDF specification states that items in this array assume a value of "None" if no value has been provided.
Items in this array may take one of the following valid values:
None
Hidden
Dotted
Dashed
Solid
Double
Groove
Ridge
Inset
Outset
If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 343, page 599.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the standard structure attributes. This is definitively detailed in:

summary.para: Create a StandardStructureAttributesElement wrapping an Atom. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns the Atom to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the Atom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.StandardStructureAttributesElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new StandardStructureAttributesElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the structure element dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 323, page 558.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 355, page 721.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because OutlineItemElement.EntrySE, StructureElementElement.EntryP and StructureElementElement.EntryRef require it to be so.

summary.para: Create a new StructureElementElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.StructureElementElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "S" entry of the structure element dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object.

The specification defines this as exensible which means that it may contain entries in addition to those defined in the specification. In fact almost all objects are extensible but the fact that it is explicitly mentioned, implies that extra entries should be regarded as normal rather than exceptional. For further details see The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: Annex E, page 673..

For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the user property dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 329, page 569.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 362, page 736.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.UserPropertyElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.WebCaptureCommandElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.summary:

summary.para: Represents the "ID" entry of the web capture content set object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 352, page 622.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 388, page 801.

summary.para: Represents the "O" entry of the web capture content set object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains Elements.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 352, page 622.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 388, page 801.

summary.para: Represents the "SI" entry of the web capture content set object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains SourceInformationElements.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one SourceInformationElement may be represented as a single SourceInformationElement rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 352, page 622.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 388, page 801.

The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 388, page 801.

summary.para: Represents the "TS" entry of the web capture content set object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object. This is encoded as a date string. For details see the StringAtom.DateToString and StringAtom.StringToDate functions.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 352, page 622.

summary.para: Create a new WebCaptureInformationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Elements.WebCaptureInformationElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the web capture page set. This is definitively detailed in:

member.summary: Whether to calcuate text widths or not. If this property is true then the ShowText function will be passed the character and advance widths for text. If it is false then null will be passed. This is quite computationally expensive so if you do not need to know the current text position on the line then you can disable this feature.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Operations.ContentStreamScanner.Warnings
member.summary: Content streams contain operators and parameters. If part of the the content stream is badly formed - for example if a parameter is missing - then an internal exception will be raised. Typically you want to move on past this and try and recover. Just because a text spacing operator is incorrect does not mean you want to abandon the whole page. Equally you do not want to completely ignore this type of error. As such, if you assign a value to this proprty, any errors or warnings will be stored here.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Operations.ContentStreamScanner.State
member.summary: The current graphics state. This broadly corresponds with the 'Graphics State' as described in the PDF Specification. The current graphics state is what is saved and restored using the PDF save and restore operators.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Operations.ContentStreamScanner.Stack
member.summary: The current graphics state stack. This broadly corresponds with the 'Graphics State' as described in the PDF Specification. The current graphics state is what is saved and restored using the PDF save and restore operators. A save pushes a copy of the current state onto the stack. A restore pops the top from the stack.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Operations.ContentStreamScanner.Text
member.summary: The current text state. Text state is not saved and restored using the PDF save and restore operators. Text state operators can occur anywhere in a content stream but typically they only occur within text blocks. A text block initializes a text matrix which allows text positioning and text showing. At the end of the text block the matrix is discarded.

member.summary: Abort the current processing. All remaining operators will be skipped.

member.summary: Process an item in a content stream and update the state to reflect the action of the item. For your own operator processing you will wish to override this function.
member.param: The owner of the stream - either a Page or Form XObject.
The contents of the stream as obtained from a call to ArrayAtom.FromContentStream or similar.
The name of the operator. For example this might be "cm" or "q".
The index of the oprator in the contents array.

member.summary: Show an item of text. If you are processing text you will want to override this function to pick up the text show operations. The parameters passed are owned by the ContentStreamScanner and will be re-used for efficiency reasons. So if you want to keep the parameters you will need make copies of them.
member.param: The character codes for the text. In general these will map to ASCII but this is not required and any encoding may be legal.
The widths of each character in 1000ths. This list is always the same size as the codes list.
The advance for each character in text units. This advance includes all text properties like character spacing and font size. This list is always the same size as the codes list.
The sum of all the values in the advances list. This is essentially the same as the text width.
The Unicode text of the codes. The text length is always the same as the size of codes list.

Some character codes do not have a single character value. For example the ligature 'fl' may be represented as one character code but the Unicode equivalent is two characters long. In this situation the 'text' parameter will contain a single character approximation and the equivalent index in the 'strings' parameter will provide the string "fl". For single character codes the index in the strings parameter will be null. This list is always the same size as the codes list.
True if the writing direction is vertical - top to bottom. False if it is horizontal - left to right.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Operations.DrawPagesOperation
member.summary: Operation to draw pages from one document onto another. This operation is in many ways similar to the Doc.AddImageDoc function. However the AddImageDoc function is not aware of state and thus it has to take each call afresh. In contrast the DrawPagesOperation is aware of state which means that, for a process drawing many pages between two documents, it can operate much more quickly.

member.summary: The level of alpha to apply to the drawn page from transparent through to fully opaque (0 to 255). If this value is null then no alpha will be applied. Default null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Operations.DrawPagesOperation.DrawPage
member.summary: Draw the current page from the source PDF document onto the current page of the destination document, returning the ID of the newly added object. The page is scaled to fill the current Rect. It is transformed using the current Transform. Many field and annotation types can only exist as a simple rectangle with sides parallel to the page borders. For this reason you should be cautious about the transforms you use when specifying that annotations should be copied. A transform which involves scale and translation will be fine but one involving rotation and skew factors may result in unusual output if the field or annotation does not support this combination. Pages may be rotated. As such, when drawing one page onto another, you may wish to copy the Page.Rotation from the source page to the destination page. More complex example code to de-rotate a page may be found under the documentation for the Page.Rotation.
member.returns: The ID of the newly added object.

member.summary: The quality of compression to use when automatically compressing after the effect is applied.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Operations.EffectOperation.Apply(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Objects.PixMap)
member.summary: Apply effect to image.
member.param: The PixMap to which the image should be applied.

remarks.para: The effect will be applied to the PixMap. Effects normally involve wholescale changes and so it may well be necessary to change the color space and depth in order to apply the effect. If the AutoRestore property is set then the PixMap will be restored to a similar color space after processing and it will be recompressed at an appropriate quality. This default is generally what is required.

However if the AutoRestore property is not set then final output may well have different characteristics such as color space and depth. In general the final image will be uncompressed eight bit RGB no matter what was supplied.

If you are relying on particular characteristics present in the original PixMap then you should convert or recolor it after the effect has been applied. Since the final image will be left uncompressed you will likely want to recompress it using an apppopriate schema.

member.summary: Gets a color conversion pipe mapping from the provided color space and page to the destination space and intent of the RecolorOperation. Pipes are owned by the RecolorOperation which means that repeated pipe requests will use cached pipes rather than recreating the same conversion over and over again. However this does also mean that at the point at which the RecolorOperation is disposed of, all owned pipes will also be disposed of. So you should only use your pipe inside the using statement that contains the RecolorOperation.

member.summary: Prepare document for drawing at the fragment location. After calling this function you can add content overlaying the fragment. For example you might call Doc.FillRect to overlay it. The Doc.Page, Doc.Rect and Doc.Transform may all be changed as a result of calling this method. Text is drawn at a height of one point, using a transformation matrix to scale it up. member.summary: Create an array of Atoms from a byte array containing a sequence of PDF objects. The returned offsets relate to the byte offsets for the start of each atom found in the stream. However the returned array may contain atoms containing other atoms so the mapping from one to the other is not as simple as it might seem. Take a returned array containing one DictAtom mapping V to the number one. The index will contain three offsets - the DictAtom, the NameAtom "V", the NumAtom 1.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.PDFLimits.FloatDigits
member.summary: The number of digits that can be written in the fractional part of a floating point number. For example if the value was five then the smallest number which could be represented would be 0.00001. The PDF 1.4 specification limited this value to five digits. You might ask how relevant the PDF 1.4 spec is now – after all it came out in 2003 and then was superseded in 2004. However then the PDF/A spec is designed against the PDF 1.4 spec so it is not just that the document might display badly in a version of Acrobat from fifteen years ago. This value defaults to five and may be set to any value between five and thirty-eight.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.PDFLimits.Epsilon
member.summary: The smallest value that can be written out to a PDF document. This value is based around the number of digits that can be written in the fractional part of a floating point number.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.OpAtom.GetParameter(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.ArrayAtom,System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the parameter associated with the OpAtom at the specified index and validates that the atom is of the correct type. Only the top level atoms are checked. So for example, the TJ operator takes an ArrayAtom consisting of NumAtoms and StringAtoms. This function will ensure that there is one ArrayAtom available as a parameter. However it will not ensure that all items inside the array are NumAtoms or StringAtoms. If the atom is not of the correct type, is not available in the array (eg because the array is too small) or the operator is unrecognized then the return value will be null. If the operator does not take any parameters the return will be null. The Atom is the actual object in the supplied array so changing the value of the Atom will change the value in the array. If the index does not point to an OpAtom or is not inside the array bounds then an exception will be thrown. This function supports all the standard PDF operator types as defined in the PDF Specification apart from BI, ID and EI which are used for inline images. The reason these are not supported is because this sequence is read as a DictAtom with embedded data so you should never encounter it.
member.param: The array in which the OpAtom is found.
The index to the OpAtom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.OpAtom.GetParameters(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.Atoms.ArrayAtom,System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the parameters associated with the OpAtom at the specified index and validates that the atoms are of the correct type. Because the arguments are validated and the types are checked so you can rely on the fact that the returned array contains a valid number of Atoms of the correct types. Only the top level atoms are checked. So for example, the TJ operator takes an ArrayAtom consisting of NumAtoms and StringAtoms. This function will ensure that there is one ArrayAtom available as a parameter. However it will not ensure that all items inside the array are NumAtoms or StringAtoms. Also resource lookups are not done so, for example, it is not checked that a font name actualy exists in the font resource dictionay. If the operator takes no parameters a zero length array will be returned. If the operator parameters are incorrect or if the operator is not recognized then the return value will be null. In this unusual situation you may wish to set the to whitespace to remove the invalid operator from the content stream. While this does not fix the underlying problem, it will at least prevent applications like Acrobat from reporting an error.
member.param: The array in which the OpAtom is found.
The index to the OpAtom.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield
member.summary: The FireShield settings that dynamically determine the file access that should be allowed for HTML conversion. FireShield lets you dynamically assign file permissions at runtime, to ensure that your HTML engine only accesses the locations you want. You can provide rules so that each request can be assigned custom rights and permissions, dependent on the type of conversion.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement
member.summary: The enforcement policy for the file access rules.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement.None
member.summary: No enforcement of the access rules.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement.Deny
member.summary: Prohibit access if the rules do not specify that access should be allowed. Always report an error if this happens.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement.Mask
member.summary: Prohibit access if the rules do not specify that access should be allowed. Attempt to continue the operation without error.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement.Log
member.summary: If the rules do not specify that access should be allowed, allow it but also log the file path.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Enabled
member.summary: Whether FireShield is enabled. Default is true.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Policy
member.summary:
File access enforcement for the worker process. This property allows you to specify the type of action that should be taken if the HTML engine attempts to access a resource to which it is not allowed. You can choose from the following options:
None - No enforcement of the access rules.
Deny - Prohibit access if the rules do not specify that access should be allowed. Always report an error if this happens.
Mask - Prohibit access if the rules do not specify that access should be allowed. Attempt to continue the operation without error.
Log - If the rules do not specify that access should be allowed, allow it, but also log the file path via the Log property.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Rules
member.summary: File access rules for the worker process. To determine whether access is allowed to a specific path, the rules are evaluated in sequence. A path may match with multiple rules and it is the final evaluated access type at the end of the sequence, which determines the access level. Rules are case insensitive. At the start of processing the evaluated access type is Deny. This means that, by default, all file access is denied. For each rule, if the file path starts with the rule path and the file name matches the pattern, then the rule access type is assigned to the evaluated access type. In this way you can set up a rule sequence which matches on a general level but then denies on a specific level. For example you might allow access to all files in a folder but then deny access to .aspx files within that folder.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XHtmlFireShield.Log
member.summary: File access log for the worker process. In the event that the Policy is set to Log, files to which access should be denied, are reported via this property.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette
member.summary: A palette of different colors that may be used. This class allows you to specify how to select colors when image colors are reduced, for example when exporting as an indexed color image.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition
member.summary: The type of palette.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Adaptive
member.summary: An optimized Octree algorithm for fast, high quality color reduction.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.WebSafe
member.summary: A fixed number of colors compatible with Web colors.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Windows
member.summary: A fixed number of colors compatible with Windows colors.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Macintosh
member.summary: A fixed number of colors compatible with Macintosh colors.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Uniform
member.summary: A set of colors uniformly distributed throughout the color space.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Grayscale
member.summary: Use only grayscale colors.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.BlackAndWhite
member.summary: Only two colors: black and white.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Exact
member.summary: Same as Adaptive but optimized to ensure an exact color match wherever possible.

summary.para: XPalette constructor. Create a default Adaptive palette with 256 colors.
The type of palette. This property reflects the set of colors that may be used. For example you may wish to select uniformly from the RGB color space or perhaps only from shades of gray.

The palette data If you want to use a raw palette derived from some source other than file then provide the raw data using this property. You may obtain such information by reading an .act file into memory. Raw palettes consist of an array of 768 bytes holding 256 RGB triplets.
The palette fixed colors. Add fixed colors to the palette when you want certain colors to be present in the palette.

Whether to dither colors when exporting. When images are exported at a reduced color depth, they can be dithered. Dithering uses a scattering of pixels of different colors to approximate colors that are not available. In general it is a good idea to dither images like photographs which contain smooth gradations of colors. It is best not to dither 'Posterized' images containing blocks of colors.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XPalette.Size
member.summary: The target number of colors in the palette.

member.summary: The default document size for documents that do not specify a size.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf12.XReadOptions.ShrinkToFit
member.summary: Whether to try and determine the document size based on the size of the content. Some formats such as SVG contain a viewport wrapper and then a viewbox containing content. The size of the viewport can be specified - much the same as specifying the size of paper something should be printed on. However similarly you can specify the size of the content without specifying the size of the viewport - much the same as saying that the drawing is a certain size without dictating the size of the paper. This is quite a common situation for web output where you want the content to be drawn in a browser window and you do not know what size the user will select for that window. If this property is set to true, the page size will be set to be the same as the content viewbox. This effectively shinks the page to fit the content avoiding excessive white space or clipping. If this property is set to false then the document size is taken from the DefaultRect property and the content is centered on this page. The viewbox size is inserted as the page ArtBox for possible use at a later stage.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.ArrayElement`1.#ctor
member.summary: Create an empty ArrayElement<T>. The Element created by this default constructor is empty - it has no Atom within it. Before use an Atom must be Assigned or Created. In practice it is easiest to do this using one of the other constructors.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.ArrayElement`1.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Create a ArrayElement<T> wrapping an Atom. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns the Atom to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the Atom.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.AtomicArrayElement`1
member.summary:
Class AtomicArrayElement.
This class represents an array of atomic elements. By atomic, we mean elements that can be directly represented using a .NET equivalent such as a string or int. On the PDF side the elements that are acceptable may be types such as StringAtom or NameAtom. The set of acceptable types may be indicated using the AtomicTypes property. Since it is an array, the core Atom this class is created from should be an ArrayAtom.
member.typeparam: Can be string, int, double, double? or bool.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element
member.summary: An Element is a specialization wrapper around an Atom designed to expose aspects of that Atom in a structured manner. Different subclasses of Element are used to represent the different objects defined in the Adobe PDF Specification. In general there is one Element subclass for each object table in the PDF Specification.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.#ctor
member.summary: Create a new Element. The different constructors allow different ways of creating an Element. Some are used for wrapping existing Atoms or IndirectObjects and others are for creating new ones. The constructor taking a relation Element creates a new object in the document - it is typically the constructor you will want to use. Do not specify creation options unless you have very specific needs. However for your first Element - one you can use as a relation for the others - you will need to wrap an existing IndirectObject inside an Element. For this you might use code of the following form "CatalogElement root = new CatalogElement(doc.ObjectSoup.Catalog)". The parameterless constructor allows you to create an empty Element. By empty we mean it has no contents - no Atom within it. So before use an Atom must be Assigned or Created. In practice it is easiest to do this using one of the other constructors. The atom and host constructor is used to wrap an existing Atom. It creates an Element and then Assigns the Atom to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the Atom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.Create(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)

summary.para: Create a new Atom for this Element. The process of Element creation works in three stages. First the Element needs to be created using the default constructor. Secondly an Atom needs to be provided for the Element. Finally the values of the Element need to be assigned.
The Create method creates a new Atom of appropriate type. This is distinct from the Assign method which allows for the adoption of an existing Atom obtained via some other source.

Each Element has its own properties, some of which may be mandatory. The creation of an Atom does not provide any of these properties. After creation the values of the Element need to be appropriately assigned using the properties prefixed with 'Item'.
Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is created is of the correct type.

member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Element.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an IndirectObject to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing IndirectObject to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that IndirectObjects are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Indirect Object to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign an IndirectObject which contains a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: The IndirectObject to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.Host
member.summary: Gets the host IndirectObject. The host is specified during construction or in a later call to Assign. The host is primarily used to indicate the document to which the Element belongs. As such it can be any IndirectObject in the document. However it is often useful to choose one which is closely associated with the Atom provided. For example, if you create an Element from an IndirectObject, the Host can be itself.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.Ref
member.summary: Gets any RefAtom that is part of this Element. When an Atom is provided during construction, this may be a reference to an IndirectObject rather than a direct reference to an Atom. If this is the case then the reference needs to be resolved through to an Atom. This property stores the original RefAtom and the Atom property stores the resolved Atom - usually a DictAtom. If the provided Atom is not a RefAtom then this property will be null.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.Atom
member.summary: Gets any Atom that is part of this Element. When an Atom is provided during construction, this may be a reference to an IndirectObject rather than a direct reference to an Atom. If this is the case then the reference needs to be resolved through to an Atom. This property stores the resolved Atom - usually a DictAtom but occasionally other types for some specific types of Element. However this property will never be a RefAtom as all references have been resolved.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.RefOrAtom
member.summary: Gets the Atom that was used to create this Element. When an Atom is provided during construction, this may be a reference to an IndirectObject rather than a direct reference to an Atom. If this is the case then the reference needs to be resolved through to an Atom. The Ref property stores the RefAtom, if one was provided. The Atom property stores the resolved Atom. This property will return the Ref if it is not null, or the Atom if it is.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.Object

When an Atom is provided during construction, this may be a reference to an IndirectObject rather than a direct reference to an Atom. If this is the case then this property stores the referenced IndirectObject. If the provided Atom is not a RefAtom then this property will be null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element.Validate(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Validation)

summary.para: Validate this object and report any inconsistencies. The validation of one object involves validating the properties of the object. Since the properties are often objects themselves, the process can be quite involved.

member.param: The Validation object which will receive validation results and progress.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This property represents the "Metadata" entry of the Element.
It is an optional entry for all Dictionaries or Streams as defined as part of the PDF 1.4 specification.
A MetadataStreamElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 3.27, page 23.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.ElementFactories
member.summary: Class ElementFactories. This static class contains a set of static factory methods for creating Elements. The reason you may need a factory method is because you may not know the type of Element you want to create at compile time. For example documents often contain annotations which float over the page. Each type of annotation is represented by a different type of Elemment. However, until you read the document, you will not know if those annotations are stamps or lines or fields or any other type of annotation. Using a factory method allows the structure of the object to be examined and a sensible Element type allocated to it. Different factory methods are appropriate at different times. For example the creation of annotations may require a different logic to the creation of actions.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.ElementFactories.AutodetectFactory(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject,System.Object)
member.summary: Autodetect Factory. This is used for the creation of specific types of Element based on the content of the Atom. Many Atoms have specific Type or Subtype fields which are used to indicate the precise variant of Element. If these are present, which in many cases they are, then a sensible choice can be made as to the type of Element to create. Even when these are not present sometimes it is possible to detect the type from specific combinations of entries found in the Atom. However not all specializations can be auto-detected as not all require this type of identification element. If this is the case then the return value will be a generic Element.
member.param: The atom from which the Element should be created.
The host object. This can be any IndirectObject in the document but it is useful to specify one with which the atom is closely associated.
A reference which may be used to pass context.
