member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Type4ShadingElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "BitsPerCoordinate" entry of the type 4 shading dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an integer representing a PDF numeric object.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 82, page 189.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 81, page 236.

summary.para: Represents the "Decode" entry of the type 4 shading dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains doubles, representing PDF numeric objects.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 82, page 189.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 81, page 237.

summary.para: Represents the "Function" entry of the type 4 shading dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains FunctionElements.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one FunctionElement may be represented as a single FunctionElement rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 82, page 190.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 81, page 237.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 82, page 189.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 81, page 237.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the type 5 shading dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 83, page 193.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 82, page 240.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because it is also a StreamElement and these are always indirect objects.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Type5ShadingElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new Type5ShadingElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Type5ShadingElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the xobject. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 201.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because it is also a StreamElement and these are always indirect objects.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.XObjectElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new XObjectElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.XObjectElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.EmbeddedFontStreamElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new EmbeddedFontStreamElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.EmbeddedFontStreamElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the font dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 254.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because GraphicsStateParameterElement.EntryFont requires it to be so.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.FontElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new FontElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.FontElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 112, page 258.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.HalftoneElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.GroupAttributesElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "TR" entry of the soft-mask dictionary object.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the action dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 193, page 414.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the appearance characteristics dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 189, page 409.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 192, page 496.

member.summary: Create an empty AppearanceCharacteristicsElement. The Element created by this default constructor is empty - it has no Atom within it. Before use an atom must be Assigned or Created. In practice it is easiest to do this using one of the other constructors.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.AppearanceCharacteristicsElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)

summary.para: Create a AppearanceCharacteristicsElement wrapping an Atom. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns the Atom to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the Atom.

member.param: The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
An IndirectObject. This can be any IndirectObject from the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with the Atom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.AppearanceCharacteristicsElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)

summary.para: Create a AppearanceCharacteristicsElement wrapping an IndirectObject. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns the IndirectObject to it. The result is a specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the IndirectObject.

member.param: The IndirectObject to be assigned to this Element.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.AppearanceCharacteristicsElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new AppearanceCharacteristicsElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.AppearanceCharacteristicsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

S
C

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CertificateSeedValueElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new CertificateSeedValueElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CertificateSeedValueElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Type" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. If provided, this item must always take the value "SVCert".
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 449.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 545.

summary.para: Represents the "Ff" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an integer representing a PDF numeric object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of 0 if no value has been provided.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 449.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 545.

summary.para: Represents the "Subject" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 449.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 545.

summary.para: Represents the "SubjectDN" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.7 specification.
It contains an array which contains Elements.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 450.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 546.

summary.para: Represents the "KeyUsage" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.7 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects. This is encoded as a string using single byte ASCII encoding.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 450.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 546.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 450.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 547.

summary.para: Represents the "OID" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 450.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 547.

summary.para: Represents the "URL" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object. This is encoded as a string using single byte ASCII encoding.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 451.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 547.

summary.para: Represents the "URLType" entry of the certificate seed value dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.7 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "Browser" if no value has been provided.

The specification defines this as exensible which means that it may contain entries in addition to those defined in the specification. In fact almost all objects are extensible but the fact that it is explicitly mentioned, implies that extra entries should be regarded as normal rather than exceptional. For further details see The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: Annex E, page 673..
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 235, page 451.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 238, page 547.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CollectionElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new CollectionElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CollectionElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the collection field dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 157, page 372.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 155, page 448.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 8.8, page 30.

summary.para: Represents the "S" entry of the collection sort dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF name objects.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 158, page 373.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 156, page 449.

summary.para: Represents the "A" entry of the collection sort dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains bool representing a PDF boolean objects. The PDF specification states that items in this array assume a value of true if no value has been provided.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one bool may be represented as a single bool rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 158, page 373.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 156, page 449.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the collection split dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 158, page 450.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 8.6b, page 31.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CollectionSplitElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new CollectionSplitElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CollectionSplitElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.FDFElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new FDFElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.FDFElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

Represents the "Encoding" entry of the fdf dictionary object.

It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "PDFDocEncoding" if no value has been provided.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the fdf field dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 246, page 461.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 249, page 559.

summary.para: Represents the "V" entry of the fdf field dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of five different types:
1) A string representing a PDF name object.
2) An array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
3) A Null.
4) A SignatureElement.
5) A StreamElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 246, page 461.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the fdf page dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 248, page 463.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 251, page 561.

summary.para: Represents the "V" entry of the field dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of five different types:
1) A string representing a PDF name object.
2) An array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
3) A Null.
4) A SignatureElement.
5) A StreamElement.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.FixedPrintElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Create a new FormFieldAdditionalActionsElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.FormFieldAdditionalActionsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.IconFitElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "F" entry of the import-data action object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a FileSpecificationElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 240, page 456.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 243, page 552.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Create a new InkAnnotationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.InteractiveFormElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the line annotation. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 175, page 398.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 178, page 482.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.MeasureElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the named action. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 212, page 427.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.NavigationNodeElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the outline dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 152, page 368.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 150, page 442.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because CatalogElement.EntryOutlines and OutlineItemElement.EntryParent require it to be so.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.OutlineElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new OutlineElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.OutlineElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the page object additional-actions dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.PageObjectAdditionalActionsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.ProjectedCoordinateSystemElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Create a new ProjectionAnnotationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Represents the "QuadPoints" entry of the redaction annotation object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains doubles, representing PDF numeric objects.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 192, page 413.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 195, page 501.

summary.para: Represents the "IC" entry of the redaction annotation object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains doubles, representing PDF numeric objects. Items in this array should have a minimum value of 0 and a maximum of 1.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 192, page 413.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 195, page 501.

summary.para: Represents the "RO" entry of the redaction annotation object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a FormXObjectElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 192, page 413.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 195, page 501.

summary.para: Represents the "OverlayText" entry of the redaction annotation object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 192, page 413.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 195, page 501.

summary.para: Represents the "Repeat" entry of the redaction annotation object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a bool representing a PDF boolean object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of false if no value has been provided.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 192, page 413.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 195, page 501.

summary.para: Represents the "DA" entry of the redaction annotation object.
It is defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 192, page 413.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 195, page 501.

summary.para: Represents the "Q" entry of the redaction annotation object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.

It contains an integer representing a PDF numeric object. It should have a minimum value of 0 and a maximum of 2. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of 0 if no value has been provided.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 192, page 414.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 195, page 501.

summary.para: Represents the "D" entry of the remote go-to action object.

This property may contain one of three different types:

For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 200, page 419.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 203, page 508.

The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 203, page 509.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 200, page 419.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the rendition action. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 214, page 428.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 218, page 520.
