member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.RequirementElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.RichMediaActivationElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Type" entry of the richmediaactivation dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.7 Extension Level 3 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. If provided, this item must always take the value "RichMediaActivation".
For definitive details see:

para.a: Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.50a, page 79.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 335, page 698.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.RichMediaActivationElement.EntryCondition
member.summary:
Represents the "Condition" entry of the richmediaactivation dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.7 Extension Level 3 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "XA" if no value has been provided.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
XA
PO
PV
For definitive details see:
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.50a, page 79.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 335, page 698.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the richmediaanimation dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 337, page 699.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.50c, page 81.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.RichMediaInstanceElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new RichMediaInstanceElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.RichMediaInstanceElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the richmediaparams dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.51c, page 90.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the richmediasettings dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 334, page 697.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.RichMediaSettingsElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new RichMediaSettingsElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.RichMediaSettingsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the signature dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 467.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 565.

summary.para: Create a new SignatureElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.SignatureElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Type" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. If provided, this item must always take the value "Sig".
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 467.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 565.

summary.para: Represents the "Filter" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object.

The specification defines this as exensible which means that it may contain entries in addition to those defined in the specification. In fact almost all objects are extensible but the fact that it is explicitly mentioned, implies that extra entries should be regarded as normal rather than exceptional. For further details see The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: Annex E, page 673..
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 467.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 565.

summary.para: Represents the "SubFilter" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.3 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object.

The specification defines this as exensible which means that it may contain entries in addition to those defined in the specification. In fact almost all objects are extensible but the fact that it is explicitly mentioned, implies that extra entries should be regarded as normal rather than exceptional. For further details see The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: Annex E, page 673..

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 467.

summary.para: Represents the "Contents" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 468.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 255, page 565.

summary.para: Represents the "Cert" entry of the signature dictionary object.
It is defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF string objects. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 252, page 468.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.SignatureValidationRelatedInformationElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Create a new TargetElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.TargetElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

Represents the "R" entry of the target dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
P
C
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 202, page 420.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 205, page 510.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 202, page 420.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the transform parameters dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; page 470.

R

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the viewer preferences dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 150, page 362.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 147, page 435.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 8.1, page 28.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.ViewerPreferencesElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the 3D activation dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 299, page 514.

summary.para: Create a new D3DActivationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.D3DActivationElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.D3DBackgroundElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Create a new D3DCrossSectionElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.D3DCrossSectionElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.D3DMeasurementElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the 3D reference dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 303, page 519.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 314, page 648.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.D3DReferenceElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.D3DUnitsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the 3D view dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 304, page 521.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 344, page 707.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.39, page 57.
Adobe Supplement to the ISO 32000, BaseVersion: 1.7, ExtensionLevel: 3; Table: 9.51f, page 93.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the media clip data dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 274, page 492.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 285, page 617.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.MediaPermissionsElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.

summary.para: Represents the "Start" entry of the movie activation dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of three different types:
1) An integer representing a PDF numeric object. It should have a minimum value of 0.
2) A string representing a PDF string object. This string contains raw byte data. So it looks like a string but really it is just a wrapper for data.
3) An array which contains Elements.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 296, page 508.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 307, page 635.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 296, page 508.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.MovieActivationElement.EntryMode
member.summary:
Represents the "Mode" entry of the movie activation dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "Once" if no value has been provided.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
Once
Open
Repeat

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the movie dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 295, page 508.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 306, page 635.

summary.para: Create a new MovieElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.MovieElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the rendition mh/be dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 267, page 489.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 278, page 613.

The PDF specification states that items in this array assume a value of "an empty array" if no value has been provided.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 292, page 504.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 303, page 631.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.SoundObjectStreamElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.

member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.MetadataStreamElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new MetadataStreamElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.MetadataStreamElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Type" entry of the metadata stream object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. This item must always be provided and must always take the value "Metadata".
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 315, page 549.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 347, page 711.

It contains a string representing a PDF name object. This item must always be provided and must always take the value "XML".
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 315, page 549.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 347, page 711.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the namespace dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 356, page 725.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because AttributeObjectElement.EntryNS, NamespaceElement.EntryRoleMapNS and StructureElementElement.EntryNS require it to be so.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the output intent dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 365, page 633.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 401, page 814.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.OutputIntentElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.SeparationElement.#ctor(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.Element,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.CreationOptions)

summary.para: Create a new SeparationElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. So if an IndirectObject is not required then a plain Atom will be used. However if the Element is of a type which requires it to be an IndirectObject, or if the options indicate it, then an IndirectObject containing an Atom will be used.

member.param: An Element. This can be any Element in the Soup but ideally should be one closely associated with this Element.

Options related to creation. For example this allows you to determine whether the Element should be created using an IndirectObject rather than just an Atom. If not provided a default set of options is used.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.SeparationElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "Pages" entry of the separation dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains PageObjectElements.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 364, page 632.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 400, page 813.

summary.para: Represents the "DeviceColorant" entry of the separation dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of two different types:
1) A string representing a PDF name object.
2) A string representing a PDF string object.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 364, page 632.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 400, page 813.

summary.para: Represents the "ColorSpace" entry of the separation dictionary object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains an array which contains ColorSpaceElements.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 364, page 633.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 400, page 813.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the source information dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 355, page 623.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 391, page 803.

summary.para: Represents the "AU" entry of the source information dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
This property may contain one of two different types:
1) A string representing a PDF string object. This is encoded as a string using single byte ASCII encoding.
2) An UrlAliasElement.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 355, page 623.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 391, page 803.

member.summary:
Represents the "Placement" entry of the standard layout attributes object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object. The PDF specification states that this item assumes a value of "Inline" if no value has been provided.
This item may take one of the following valid values:
Block
Inline
Before
Start
End

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.StandardLayoutAttributesElement.EntryBorderStyle
member.summary:
Represents the "BorderStyle" entry of the standard layout attributes object.
It is an optional entry defined as part of the PDF 1.5 specification.
It contains an array which contains strings, representing PDF name objects. The PDF specification states that items in this array assume a value of "None" if no value has been provided.
Items in this array may take one of the following valid values:
None
Hidden
Dotted
Dashed
Solid
Double
Groove
Ridge
Inset
Outset
If you read the specification you will see that an array of one string may be represented as a single string rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 343, page 599.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 378, page 772.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the standard structure attributes. This is definitively detailed in:

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the structure element dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 323, page 558.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 355, page 721.

summary.para: This class is always an indirect object because OutlineItemElement.EntrySE, StructureElementElement.EntryP and StructureElementElement.EntryRef require it to be so.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.StructureElementElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "S" entry of the structure element dictionary object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.
It contains a string representing a PDF name object.

The specification defines this as exensible which means that it may contain entries in addition to those defined in the specification. In fact almost all objects are extensible but the fact that it is explicitly mentioned, implies that extra entries should be regarded as normal rather than exceptional. For further details see The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: Annex E, page 673..

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.

summary.para: Create a new StructureTreeRootElement for use in the same soup as the relation. This constructor creates an Element and then Assigns a new Atom or IndirectObject to it. The result is a new, blank specialized Element which can be used to examine or modify the contents of the new Atom. Some Elements always need to be IndirectObjects, others can be simply Atoms. member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.StructureTreeRootElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.UserPropertyElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
This class represents the web capture command dictionary. This is definitively detailed in:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 357, page 624.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 393, page 804.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.WebCaptureCommandElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

summary.para: Represents the "SI" entry of the web capture content set object.
It is a required entry defined as part of the PDF 1.0 specification.

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 352, page 622.

If you read the specification you will see that an array of one integer may be represented as a single integer rather than an array. However we always present this property as an array to simplify the interface. It is only if you add or remove items in the array, that the underlying representation will be changed.
For definitive details see:

para.a: The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-1:2008 PDF 1.7; Table: 354, page 622.
The ISO PDF Specification, ISO 32000-2:2017 PDF 2.0; Table: 390, page 802.

summary.para: Clears any cached Element items.

Elements in properties are cached so that the Element you assign to a property is the same as the one you retrieve when you later get that property. However it is possible that sometimes this behavior is not what you want. For example suppose you assign a DeviceColorSpaceElement to a property and then later change the underlying Atom so that it is really a CalRGBColorSpace. In this situation the retrieved ColorSpaceElement will continue to be interpreted as a DeviceColorSpaceElement and an invalid one at that. What you really want to do here is to clear the cached Element thus allowing the property to be regenerated as a CalRGBColorSpace. This function clears the cached Elements to allow this to happen.
