member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Elements.WebCaptureInformationElement.Assign(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.Atom,WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject)
member.summary: Assign an Atom to this Element. The process of assignment allows an existing Atom to be viewed through the lens of a particular type of Element. It is important to ensure that Atoms are assigned to appropriate types of Element. For example, while is is possible to assign a Page Atom to an Image Element, such an assignment is not going to produce any useful view of the data. In addition, some assignments cannot be made at all. This occurs if if the underlying atom types are inconsistent. For example a ColorSpaceElement is based around an ArrayAtom, so attempting to assign a DictAtom will result in failure. Classes that inherit from this one may wish to override this function to ensure that the Atom type that is provided is acceptable.
member.param: An IndirectObject closely associated with this Atom - ideally the one that contains it.
The Atom to be assigned to this Element.
member.returns: Whether the assignment was made successfully.
member.exception: Thrown if the atom or host provided is null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.OpAtom.GetParameter(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.ArrayAtom,System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the parameter associated with the OpAtom at the specified index and validates that the atom is of the correct type. Only the top level atoms are checked. So for example, the TJ operator takes an ArrayAtom consisting of NumAtoms and StringAtoms. This function will ensure that there is one ArrayAtom available as a parameter. However it will not ensure that all items inside the array are NumAtoms or StringAtoms. If the atom is not of the correct type, is not available in the array (eg because the array is too small) or the operator is unrecognized then the return value will be null. If the operator does not take any parameters the return will be null. The Atom is the actual object in the supplied array so changing the value of the Atom will change the value in the array. If the index does not point to an OpAtom or is not inside the array bounds then an exception will be thrown. This function supports all the standard PDF operator types as defined in the PDF Specification apart from BI, ID and EI which are used for inline images. The reason these are not supported is because this sequence is read as a DictAtom with embedded data so you should never encounter it.
member.param: The array in which the OpAtom is found.
The index to the OpAtom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.OpAtom.GetParameters(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Atoms.ArrayAtom,System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the parameters associated with the OpAtom at the specified index and validates that the atoms are of the correct type. Because the arguments are validated and the types are checked so you can rely on the fact that the returned array contains a valid number of Atoms of the correct types. Only the top level atoms are checked. So for example, the TJ operator takes an ArrayAtom consisting of NumAtoms and StringAtoms. This function will ensure that there is one ArrayAtom available as a parameter. However it will not ensure that all items inside the array are NumAtoms or StringAtoms. Also resource lookups are not done so, for example, it is not checked that a font name actualy exists in the font resource dictionay. If the operator takes no parameters a zero length array will be returned. If the operator parameters are incorrect or if the operator is not recognized then the return value will be null. In this unusual situation you may wish to set the to whitespace to remove the invalid operator from the content stream. While this does not fix the underlying problem, it will at least prevent applications like Acrobat from reporting an error.
member.param: The array in which the OpAtom is found.
The index to the OpAtom.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Annotation.FieldBorderColor
member.summary: The border color of the field. This color must be grayscale, RGB or CMYK. If it is null then the border is transparent. This property is only valid if this annotation is associated with a form field. When you set this property a clone of the XColor you assign is created to avoid one XColor being shared by multiple annotations. After changing this property you will need to call to realize the change.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Annotation.Border
member.summary: The border appearance. This property is a three or four element array. The first three elements describe the horizontal corner radius, the vertical corner radius and the border width. If the corners are zero then the border has rectangular rather than rounded corners. If the border width is zero then there is no border. The last optional element is a dash array to be used in drawing dashed borders. This conforms to the standard dash array format which indicates alternatingly the length of lines and gaps. So [2 1] would indicate two on, one off, two on, one off... Longer arrays can be used for more complex dash patterns. If this property is null then a solid rectangular border of width one will be drawn. This is equivalent to the following code: annot.Border = (ArrayAtom)Atom.FromString("[0 0 1"); // C#annot.Border = DirectCast(Atom.FromString("[0 0 1]"), ArrayAtom) ' VB.NET After changing this property you will need to call to realize the change.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Catalog.GetEmbeddedFiles
member.summary:
Gets all the embedded files in this document.
PDF documents can contain a set of named files. These files can then be referenced by name elsewhere in the document.
The most common case in which named files are used is in the case of PDF portfolios. Adobe now uses the name Portfolio for this type of document but in the PDF specification they are known as Portable Collections. While the names may vary two are the same.
PDF Portfolios appear as one PDF document but actually contain many. Typically the first document represents the visible face of the collection when opened. After the collection is open you can switch between the embedded PDFs.
PDF portfolios can be used to represent a folder of PDFs. For example you might find a portable collection being used to display multiple emails within a single PDF Portfolio.
member.returns: All the files embedded in the document.

Choice fields such as Combo boxes and Lists have a value selected from one of their Options. However it is possible to specify an export value which is different from the value of field. member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.FileSpecification.Platform
member.summary:
The default platform being used for the file specification.
For historic reasons PDF has supported multiple different files for multiple different platforms. This was appropriate when files were often non-interoperable and would not port easily between machines.
Fortunately this state of affairs is now unusual and only the default "UF" platform is commonly used. Adobe do not specify what the initials stand for, but it is likely to be Unicode File, though it could be Universal File or URL File.
While you are unlikely to wish to create documents which use these obsolescent platforms, you may find old documents that use them. This method allows you to access information specified by platform. Appropriate selectors are "UF", "F", "DOS", "Mac" or "Unix" as per the descriptions in the Adobe PDF Specification. You can use the Platforms property to deterine which are being used.
The defaut of "UF" provides access via the standard settings as specified in the PDF 1.7 specification.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.FileSpecification.Uri
member.summary:
The URI to the file.
For the default platform, attempting to set this property to a value which is nov a valid URI will result in an exception being thrown. To convert a standard Windows path to a URI use (new System.Uri(path).AbsouteUri.
For some values of the Platform property (eg Mac, DOS, Unix) raw file paths can be used. However these are obsolete and while you may see PDFs which contain them, you would be inadvised to generate new documents containing these structures.

summary.para: The embedded file if one has been embedded in the PDF.
If a file has not been embedded then the URL needs to be intepreted in the context of the current PDF to locate the external file.
Setting this property will clear the EmbeddedFiles property if one is present.
This property references another in the Doc. So if this object is not part of a Doc then this property will always be null.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.FileSpecification.EmbeddedFiles

summary.para: The set of embedded files if a set has been embedded in the PDF.

Normally a file specification will refer to one file. However in some situations it may be necessary to allow it to refer to multiple. For example if a CMYK image is available as four color separations then it may be useful to be able to embed four different files to make up the whole data set. Each file will need a name so this property reflects both the name and the content of each file.

If the EmbeddedFiles property has a value, then the first file in the array should always be the same as the EmbeddedFile property. For this reason setting this property will also set the EmbeddedFile property to be equal to the first file in the array. If there are no items in the array then the EmbeddedFile property will be cleared.

member.para: This property references other objects in the Doc. So if this object is not part of a Doc then this property will always be null.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.FontObject.FontBBox
member.summary:
The bounding box for the glyphs in this font. This corresponds to the xMin, xMax, yMin and yMax entries in the 'head' TrueType table.
The PDF format only supports a limited range of metrics so FontObjects read from PDF may contain some approximations compared with 'live' FontObjects which have been added using the Doc.AddFont or Doc.EmbedFont methods.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.FontObject.FontLineSpacing
member.summary:
The line spacing for the glyphs in this font.
This broadly reflects the distance in 1000ths between the bottom of the lowest descender and the top of the highest ascender on two subsequent lines. We follow Microsoft best practice on this metric and vary the calculations depending on whether bit 7 of the fsSelection entry in the 'OS/2' TrueType table is set or not. However it is worth noting that many items of software including Microsoft flagship products do not.
The PDF format only supports a limited range of metrics so FontObjects read from PDF may contain some approximations compared with 'live' FontObjects which have been added using the Doc.AddFont or Doc.EmbedFont methods.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject.Transcode
member.summary: Transcodes and reloads the IndirectObject. Normally transcoding takes place automatically as objects are added. However sometimes changes occur after the even which may result in core aspects of the object changing. These changes may require caches to be regenerated or even an entirely new object to be created - one which better represents the new underlying structure of the PDF data. This is particualy the caes for the FontObject class which implements a lot of caching and is often dependent on other objcts in the soup. If transcoding results in a new object being created it will displace the current object from the soup. As such you will noremlly discard the old reference if a new IndirectObject is returned.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject.GetHashCode
member.summary: A hash code for the IndirectObject.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.IndirectObject.GetHashCode(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.ComparisonType)
member.summary: A hash code derived from this IndirectObject. The hash code can be made up of a variety of parts of the indirect object combined together. The ID and the Atom hash codes are derived from the value of the ID and Atom respectively. The Data hash code is made from a sample of the compressed data contained in the stream. For this reason two StreamObjects, compressed differently, will return different hash codes even if the uncompressed data is identical. The data sample is kept small - in the order of a few hundred bytes - to ensure a fast response even for very large streams.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Page.StampFormXObjects(System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Removes all FormXObjects from the page by embedding them into the content.
Most Form XObjects can be embedded in the page with no difference in page appearance. However Form XObjects such as transparency groups contain structures which cannot be represented any other way. These structures are uncommon in most documents but they do occur.
In this situation you need to decide whether a change in page appearance is acceptable and that the objects should be forcably embedded. The alternative is to skip these objects and embed only those that will not affect the page appearance.
member.param: Whether to stamp FormXObjects that may cause a change in the page appearance.
member.returns: The number of FormXObjects removed from the page.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Page.StampFormXObjects(System.Boolean,System.Int32)

Most Form XObjects can be embedded in the page with no difference in page appearance. However Form XObjects such as transparency groups contain structures which cannot be represented any other way. These structures are uncommon in most documents but they do occur.
In this situation you need to decide whether a change in page appearance is acceptable and that the objects should be forcably embedded. The alternative is to skip these objects and embed only those that will not affect the page appearance.
member.param: Whether to stamp FormXObjects that may cause a change in the page appearance.
The maximum number of levels of nested FormXObjects that should be flattened.
member.returns: The number of FormXObjects removed from the page.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Page.GetBitmap(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Layer[])
member.summary: Render one or more layers on the current page.

remarks.para: This function renders a set of layers and returns the result as a System.Drawing.Bitmap. The Bitmap covers the smallest possible area which encompasses all the layers provided.
If this Page is not in a Doc then an exception will be raised. The function will return null if the layers argument is null or empty or the output Bitmap would be smaller than one pixel in area.

Rendering options such as resolution in DPI,are taken directly from the current XRendering settings for the doc. However automatic page rotation (XRendering.AutoRotate) is disabled so that a Layer can be rendered and then re-inserted into the page as a raster copy of itself.

Note that a layer can exist on multiple pages and indeed can be rendered in the context of a page that does not contain it. However layers typically contain references to named resources which are only available in the context of a specific page. So rendering a layer in the context of a page which does not normally contain it is prone to error unless the page and layer have been specifically consructed to allow this.

member.param: The layers to be rendered.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Page.MediaBox
member.summary: The MediaBox for the page.

remarks.para: The MediaBox defines the boundaries of the physical medium on which the page may be displayed or printed. This may include bleed areas or printing marks and also parts of the medium on which printing cannot take place because of physicsal limitations of the output technology. Any PDF drawing outside the MediaBox can be safely ignored.
These boundaries may be defined directly on the Page object or they may be inherited from a parent Pages object.
A MediaBox is mandatory for all pages so this property should never be null.

Assigning a new value to this property will change the property for the current Page rather than any Pages object from which the value may have been inherited. In this way the property exhibits a copy-on-write behavior.
Attempting to assign a null value to this property will result in a NullReferenceException being thrown.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Page.CropBox
member.summary:
The CropBox for the page.
The CropBox defines the visible part of the physical medium on which the page may be displayed or printed. This is what you see as the boundary of the page when you view a document using Acrobat Reader.
These boundaries may be defined directly on the Page object or they may be inherited from a parent Pages object.
The CropBox is optional and if this property is null it is implicitly assumed to be the same as the MediaBox.
Assigning a new value to this property will change the property for the current Page rather than any Pages object from which the value may have been inherited. In this way the property exhibits a copy-on-write behavior.
Attempting to assign a null value to this property will result in a NullReferenceException being thrown. If you want to assign an effective value of null to this property you should assign it the value of the MediaBox.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Page.TrimBox
member.summary: The TrimBox for the page.

remarks.para: The TrimBox defines the intended boundaries of the page after trimming.
These boundaries are always defined directly on the Page object. If no property has been defined then this property will be null and the effective value is assumed to be that of the CropBox.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Page.ArtBox
member.summary: The ArtBox for the page.

remarks.para: The ArtBox defines the extent of meaningful content on this page.
These boundaries are always defined directly on the Page object. If no property has been defined then this property will be null and the effective value is assumed to be that of the CropBox.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.Page.BleedBox
member.summary: The BleedBox for the page.

remarks.para: The BleedBox defines the region to which the contents of the page shall be clipped when rendered in a production environment.
These boundaries are always defined directly on the Page object. If no property has been defined then this property will be null and the effective value is assumed to be that of the CropBox.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.PixMap.Rotate(System.Int32)
member.summary: Rotate the image clockwise.
member.param: The number of degrees clockwise that the image should be rotated. This must be a multiple of 90.

remarks.para: This function rotates the PixMap image clockwise. The rotation angle must be a multiple of 90. If an invalid number of degrees is specified then an ArgumentOutOfRangeException will be thrown.
An image may have an associated bit mask or soft (alpha) mask. If this is the case the associated mask will be transformed as well.

When a PixMap is drawn on a page it is scaled to fit into a particular location. The scaling is separate from the PixMap itself. Rotating by 90 or 270 degrees will swap the width and height of the PixMap. Because the scaling of drawn copies is separate from the PixMap itself, any previously drawn instances of the PixMap may appear to have an incorrect aspect ratio.
After this method has been called the PixMap will no longer be compressed. You may wish to compress it using the StreamObject.Compress method or similar.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.PixMap.Flip(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Flip the image horizontally or vertically.
member.param: Whether to flip the image horizontally.
Whether to flip the image vertically.

remarks.para: This function flips the image horizontally or vertically or both. Flipping both horizontally and vertically is equivalent to a 180 degree rotation.
An image may have an associated bit mask or soft (alpha) mask. If this is the case the associated mask will be transformed as well.
Flipping horizontally will mean that pixels that were on the far right of the image will be moved to the far left and pixels on the left will be moved to the right.
Flipping horizontally will mean that pixels that were on the top of the image will be moved to the bottom and pixels that were on the bottom will be moved to the top.
After this method has been called the PixMap will no longer be compressed. You may wish to compress it using the StreamObject.Compress method or similar.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.StreamObject.CopyDecompressedData(System.Byte[],System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Copy the decompressed binary content of the stream into a byte array. This method does not alter the content of the StreamObject so it is an efficient way of getting the decompressed data without altering the document. If the data could not be decompressed then an exception will be raised. The decompressed data is cached so that multiple calls to this function are efficient. For this reason calling this value with a null destination is an efficient way of determining the length of the decompressed stream.
member.param: The destination byte array. Default is null.
The index in the byte array at which the first byte should be written. Default is 0.
The maximum number of bytes that should be written. Default is Int.MaxValue.
member.returns: The length of the decompressed data that has been written to the array. If the destination is null then this returns the length that would have been written if a destination had been provided.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Operations.DrawPagesOperation
member.summary: Operation to draw pages from one document onto another. This operation is in many ways similar to the Doc.AddImageDoc function. However the AddImageDoc function is not aware of state and thus it has to take each call afresh. In contrast the DrawPagesOperation is aware of state which means that, for a process drawing many pages between two documents, it can operate much more quickly.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Operations.DrawPagesOperation.Alpha
member.summary: The level of alpha to apply to the drawn page from transparent through to fully opaque (0 to 255). If this value is null then no alpha will be applied. Default null.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Operations.DrawPagesOperation.DrawPage
member.summary: Draw the current page from the source PDF document onto the current page of the destination document, returning the ID of the newly added object. The page is scaled to fill the current Rect. It is transformed using the current Transform. Many field and annotation types can only exist as a simple rectangle with sides parallel to the page borders. For this reason you should be cautious about the transforms you use when specifying that annotations should be copied. A transform which involves scale and translation will be fine but one involving rotation and skew factors may result in unusual output if the field or annotation does not support this combination. Pages may be rotated. As such, when drawing one page onto another, you may wish to copy the Page.Rotation from the source page to the destination page. More complex example code to de-rotate a page may be found under the documentation for the Page.Rotation.
member.returns: The ID of the newly added object.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Operations.EffectOperation.Apply(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.Objects.PixMap)
member.summary: Apply effect to image.
member.param: The PixMap to which the image should be applied.

remarks.para: The effect will be applied to the PixMap. Effects normally involve wholescale changes and so it may well be necessary to change the color space and depth in order to apply the effect. If the AutoRestore property is set then the PixMap will be restored to a similar color space after processing and it will be recompressed at an appropriate quality. This default is generally what is required.

However if the AutoRestore property is not set then final output may well have different characteristics such as color space and depth. In general the final image will be uncompressed eight bit RGB no matter what was supplied.

If you are relying on particular characteristics present in the original PixMap then you should convert or recolor it after the effect has been applied. Since the final image will be left uncompressed you will likely want to recompress it using an apppopriate schema.

member.summary: Gets a color conversion pipe mapping from the provided color space and page to the destination space and intent of the RecolorOperation. Pipes are owned by the RecolorOperation which means that repeated pipe requests will use cached pipes rather than recreating the same conversion over and over again. However this does also mean that at the point at which the RecolorOperation is disposed of, all owned pipes will also be disposed of. So you should only use your pipe inside the using statement that contains the RecolorOperation.

The source color space atom.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield
member.summary: The FireShield settings that dynamically determine the file access that should be allowed for HTML conversion. FireShield lets you dynamically assign file permissions at runtime, to ensure that your HTML engine only accesses the locations you want. You can provide rules so that each request can be assigned custom rights and permissions, dependent on the type of conversion.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement
member.summary: The enforcement policy for the file access rules.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement.None
member.summary: No enforcement of the access rules.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement.Deny
member.summary: Prohibit access if the rules do not specify that access should be allowed. Always report an error if this happens.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement.Mask
member.summary: Prohibit access if the rules do not specify that access should be allowed. Attempt to continue the operation without error.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield.Enforcement.Log
member.summary: If the rules do not specify that access should be allowed, allow it but also log the file path.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield.Policy
member.summary:
File access enforcement for the worker process. This property allows you to specify the type of action that should be taken if the HTML engine attempts to access a resource to which it is not allowed. You can choose from the following options:
None - No enforcement of the access rules.
Deny - Prohibit access if the rules do not specify that access should be allowed. Always report an error if this happens.
Mask - Prohibit access if the rules do not specify that access should be allowed. Attempt to continue the operation without error.
Log - If the rules do not specify that access should be allowed, allow it, but also log the file path via the Log property.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield.Rules
member.summary: File access rules for the worker process. To determine whether access is allowed to a specific path, the rules are evaluated in sequence. A path may match with multiple rules and it is the final evaluated access type at the end of the sequence, which determines the access level. Rules are case insensitive. At the start of processing the evaluated access type is Deny. This means that, by default, all file access is denied. For each rule, if the file path starts with the rule path and the file name matches the pattern, then the rule access type is assigned to the evaluated access type. In this way you can set up a rule sequence which matches on a general level but then denies on a specific level. For example you might allow access to all files in a folder but then deny access to .aspx files within that folder.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XHtmlFireShield.Log
member.summary: File access log for the worker process. In the event that the Policy is set to Log, files to which access should be denied, are reported via this property.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette
member.summary: A palette of different colors that may be used. This class allows you to specify how to select colors when image colors are reduced, for example when exporting as an indexed color image.

member.name: T:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition
member.summary: The type of palette.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Adaptive
member.summary: An optimized Octree algorithm for fast, high quality color reduction.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.WebSafe
member.summary: A fixed number of colors compatible with Web colors.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Windows
member.summary: A fixed number of colors compatible with Windows colors.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Macintosh
member.summary: A fixed number of colors compatible with Macintosh colors.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Uniform
member.summary: A set of colors uniformly distributed throughout the color space.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Grayscale
member.summary: Use only grayscale colors.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.BlackAndWhite
member.summary: Only two colors: black and white.

member.name: F:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.PaletteDefinition.Exact
member.summary: Same as Adaptive but optimized to ensure an exact color match wherever possible.

summary.para: XPalette constructor. Create a default Adaptive palette with 256 colors.
The type of palette. This property reflects the set of colors that may be used. For example you may wish to select uniformly from the RGB color space or perhaps only from shades of gray.

The palette data If you want to use a raw palette derived from some source other than file then provide the raw data using this property. You may obtain such information by reading an .act file into memory. Raw palettes consist of an array of 768 bytes holding 256 RGB triplets.
The palette fixed colors. Add fixed colors to the palette when you want certain colors to be present in the palette.

Whether to dither colors when exporting. When images are exported at a reduced color depth, they can be dithered. Dithering uses a scattering of pixels of different colors to approximate colors that are not available. In general it is a good idea to dither images like photographs which contain smooth gradations of colors. It is best not to dither 'Posterized' images containing blocks of colors.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XPalette.Size
member.summary: The target number of colors in the palette.

member.summary: The default document size for documents that do not specify a size.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XReadOptions.ShrinkToFit
member.summary: Whether to try and determine the document size based on the size of the content. Some formats such as SVG contain a viewport wrapper and then a viewbox containing content. The size of the viewport can be specified - much the same as specifying the size of paper something should be printed on. However similarly you can specify the size of the content without specifying the size of the viewport - much the same as saying that the drawing is a certain size without dictating the size of the paper. This is quite a common situation for web output where you want the content to be drawn in a browser window and you do not know what size the user will select for that window. If this property is set to true, the page size will be set to be the same as the content viewbox. This effectively shinks the page to fit the content avoiding excessive white space or clipping. If this property is set to false then the document size is taken from the DefaultRect property and the content is centered on this page. The viewbox size is inserted as the page ArtBox for possible use at a later stage.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XRendering.Palette
member.summary: The palette used when reducing colors.
member.remarks:
When reducing colors, there are different ways to choose such colors. This property controls how colors are chosen. We provide the following options:
Adaptive. This palette uses fewer colors than specified if the image has limited colors. It uses an optimized Octree algorithm for fast, high quality color reduction.
WebSafe. This palette uses a fixed number of colors. is ignored.
Windows. This palette uses a fixed number of colors. is ignored.
Macintosh. This palette uses a fixed number of colors. is ignored.
Uniform. This palette specified a set of uniformly distributed colors. It only exists for 8, 27, 64, 125 and 216 colors and so the number you specify with may be reduced to accommodate this.
Grayscale. This palette uses the exact number of gray values specified in - minimum two.
Black&White. This palette always uses two colors - black and white.
Exact. This is similar to Adaptive except it is optimized to ensure an exact color match wherever possible.
When using Exact or Adaptive, you can append colors separated by colons or semicolons. These colors are fixed colors, which will always by added to the palette. See the example below.

members.member: The kerning of type. The default kerning is based on the glyph indexes and the kerning table which applies to them. This is sometimes known as format zero. There are other other types of kerning based on classes of glyphs and the relationship between ther classes. This is sometimes known as format two. In theory the two formats will produce the same result. However this depends on the accuracy with which the fonts are constructed. There are no formats one or three. As well as the standard kerning there are other forms which allow shifts perpendicular to the text flow. However this is unusual and little used and is not currently supported.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XTextStyle.CharUsage
member.summary: The usage of characters.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf11.XTextStyle.LeftMargin
member.summary: The paragraph indent (points).

members.member: The default text direction. Most Western languages have a default reading direction of left-to-right. However some other languages, notably Hebrew and Arabic, read right-to left. To further complicate matters it is quite common for languages like Hebrew to read bi-directionally - to have sections which are read left-to-right against the normal flow of text. The most common case in which this occurs is the use of numbers in text. Numbers are always read left-to-right. However it is also quite common to quote English names and again these are read in the standard English direction. This property allows you to set the default or predominant direction to be assumed for text.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Atoms.OpAtom.GetParameter(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Atoms.ArrayAtom,System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the parameter associated with the OpAtom at the specified index and validates that the atom is of the correct type. Only the top level atoms are checked. So for example, the TJ operator takes an ArrayAtom consisting of NumAtoms and StringAtoms. This function will ensure that there is one ArrayAtom available as a parameter. However it will not ensure that all items inside the array are NumAtoms or StringAtoms. If the atom is not of the correct type, is not available in the array (eg because the array is too small) or the operator is unrecognized then the return value will be null. If the operator does not take any parameters the return will be null. The Atom is the actual object in the supplied array so changing the value of the Atom will change the value in the array. If the index does not point to an OpAtom or is not inside the array bounds then an exception will be thrown. This function supports all the standard PDF operator types as defined in the PDF Specification apart from BI, ID and EI which are used for inline images. The reason these are not supported is because this sequence is read as a DictAtom with embedded data so you should never encounter it.
member.param: The array in which the OpAtom is found.
The index to the OpAtom.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Atoms.OpAtom.GetParameters(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Atoms.ArrayAtom,System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the parameters associated with the OpAtom at the specified index and validates that the atoms are of the correct type. Because the arguments are validated and the types are checked so you can rely on the fact that the returned array contains a valid number of Atoms of the correct types. Only the top level atoms are checked. So for example, the TJ operator takes an ArrayAtom consisting of NumAtoms and StringAtoms. This function will ensure that there is one ArrayAtom available as a parameter. However it will not ensure that all items inside the array are NumAtoms or StringAtoms. Also resource lookups are not done so, for example, it is not checked that a font name actualy exists in the font resource dictionay. If the operator takes no parameters a zero length array will be returned. If the operator parameters are incorrect or if the operator is not recognized then the return value will be null. In this unusual situation you may wish to set the to whitespace to remove the invalid operator from the content stream. While this does not fix the underlying problem, it will at least prevent applications like Acrobat from reporting an error.
member.param: The array in which the OpAtom is found.
The index to the OpAtom.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Annotation.FieldBackgroundColor
member.summary: The background color of the field. This color must be grayscale, RGB or CMYK. If it is null then the background is transparent. This property is only valid if this annotation is associated with a form field. When you set this property a clone of the XColor you assign is created to avoid one XColor being shared by multiple annotations. After changing this property you will need to call to realize the change.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Annotation.FieldBorderColor
member.summary: The border color of the field. This color must be grayscale, RGB or CMYK. If it is null then the border is transparent. This property is only valid if this annotation is associated with a form field. When you set this property a clone of the XColor you assign is created to avoid one XColor being shared by multiple annotations. After changing this property you will need to call to realize the change.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Annotation.Border
member.summary: The border appearance. This property is a three or four element array. The first three elements describe the horizontal corner radius, the vertical corner radius and the border width. If the corners are zero then the border has rectangular rather than rounded corners. If the border width is zero then there is no border. The last optional element is a dash array to be used in drawing dashed borders. This conforms to the standard dash array format which indicates alternatingly the length of lines and gaps. So [2 1] would indicate two on, one off, two on, one off... Longer arrays can be used for more complex dash patterns. If this property is null then a solid rectangular border of width one will be drawn. This is equivalent to the following code: annot.Border = (ArrayAtom)Atom.FromString("[0 0 1"); // C#annot.Border = DirectCast(Atom.FromString("[0 0 1]"), ArrayAtom) ' VB.NET After changing this property you will need to call to realize the change.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Catalog.GetEmbeddedFiles
member.summary:
Gets all the embedded files in this document.
PDF documents can contain a set of named files. These files can then be referenced by name elsewhere in the document.
The most common case in which named files are used is in the case of PDF portfolios. Adobe now uses the name Portfolio for this type of document but in the PDF specification they are known as Portable Collections. While the names may vary two are the same.
PDF Portfolios appear as one PDF document but actually contain many. Typically the first document represents the visible face of the collection when opened. After the collection is open you can switch between the embedded PDFs.
PDF portfolios can be used to represent a folder of PDFs. For example you might find a portable collection being used to display multiple emails within a single PDF Portfolio.
member.returns: All the files embedded in the document.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.ColorSpace.Gamma
member.summary: The gamma correction for the color space. Gamma is defined for each component of a calibrated color space. So for a CalGray color space it has one entry and for a CalRGB color space it has three. This means that for a CalGray color space this property will be a NumAtom and for a CalRGB color space it will be an ArrayAtom with three entries. Gamma is not valid for other color spaces. Each gamma entry must be positive and is generally greater than or equal to one.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Field.SetFont(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.FontObject,System.Double)
member.summary: Sets the font and font size to be used for text. Callng this function works by changing the for the field. Properties such ase the and gets the effective value which may be inherited. Calling this funtion sets the value on this item itself which will override any inherited value. Passing a font value of null will remove both the font and size from the item itself though a value may be still be present if it is inherited from a parent field or from document defaults. A zero size font indicates that the font should scale so that it fits the size of the field. Negative font heights appear the same as positive ones but are best avoided as they are likely to cause confusion. The appearance of the field is not updated until you change the or call .

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Field.GetExportValues

summary.para: The export values for this field.

Choice fields such as Combo boxes and Lists have a value selected from one of their Options. However it is possible to specify an export value which is different from the value of field. The export value will be used if the form data is exported or submitted in some way so it is purely for external use. This function allows you to get the export values from the field.
Please note that export values are only meaningful for fields of FieldType FieldType.Combo or FieldType.List and they are only relevant for form export.

member.returns: An array of strings - one for each option. The size of the array is always equal to the number of options.

The default platform being used for the file specification.
For historic reasons PDF has supported multiple different files for multiple different platforms. This was appropriate when files were often non-interoperable and would not port easily between machines.
Fortunately this state of affairs is now unusual and only the default "UF" platform is commonly used. Adobe do not specify what the initials stand for, but it is likely to be Unicode File, though it could be Universal File or URL File.
While you are unlikely to wish to create documents which use these obsolescent platforms, you may find old documents that use them. This method allows you to access information specified by platform. Appropriate selectors are "UF", "F", "DOS", "Mac" or "Unix" as per the descriptions in the Adobe PDF Specification. You can use the Platforms property to deterine which are being used.
The defaut of "UF" provides access via the standard settings as specified in the PDF 1.7 specification.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.FileSpecification.Uri
member.summary:
The URI to the file.
For the default platform, attempting to set this property to a value which is nov a valid URI will result in an exception being thrown. To convert a standard Windows path to a URI use (new System.Uri(path).AbsouteUri.
For some values of the Platform property (eg Mac, DOS, Unix) raw file paths can be used. However these are obsolete and while you may see PDFs which contain them, you would be inadvised to generate new documents containing these structures.

summary.para: The embedded file if one has been embedded in the PDF.
If a file has not been embedded then the URL needs to be intepreted in the context of the current PDF to locate the external file.
Setting this property will clear the EmbeddedFiles property if one is present.
This property references another in the Doc. So if this object is not part of a Doc then this property will always be null.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.FileSpecification.EmbeddedFiles

summary.para: The set of embedded files if a set has been embedded in the PDF.

Normally a file specification will refer to one file. However in some situations it may be necessary to allow it to refer to multiple. For example if a CMYK image is available as four color separations then it may be useful to be able to embed four different files to make up the whole data set. Each file will need a name so this property reflects both the name and the content of each file.

If the EmbeddedFiles property has a value, then the first file in the array should always be the same as the EmbeddedFile property. For this reason setting this property will also set the EmbeddedFile property to be equal to the first file in the array. If there are no items in the array then the EmbeddedFile property will be cleared.

member.summary:
The bounding box for the glyphs in this font. This corresponds to the xMin, xMax, yMin and yMax entries in the 'head' TrueType table.
The PDF format only supports a limited range of metrics so FontObjects read from PDF may contain some approximations compared with 'live' FontObjects which have been added using the Doc.AddFont or Doc.EmbedFont methods.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.FontObject.FontLineSpacing
member.summary:
The line spacing for the glyphs in this font.
This broadly reflects the distance in 1000ths between the bottom of the lowest descender and the top of the highest ascender on two subsequent lines. We follow Microsoft best practice on this metric and vary the calculations depending on whether bit 7 of the fsSelection entry in the 'OS/2' TrueType table is set or not. However it is worth noting that many items of software including Microsoft flagship products do not.
The PDF format only supports a limited range of metrics so FontObjects read from PDF may contain some approximations compared with 'live' FontObjects which have been added using the Doc.AddFont or Doc.EmbedFont methods.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.IndirectObject.Transcode
member.summary: Transcodes and reloads the IndirectObject. Normally transcoding takes place automatically as objects are added. However sometimes changes occur after the even which may result in core aspects of the object changing. These changes may require caches to be regenerated or even an entirely new object to be created - one which better represents the new underlying structure of the PDF data. This is particualy the caes for the FontObject class which implements a lot of caching and is often dependent on other objcts in the soup. If transcoding results in a new object being created it will displace the current object from the soup. As such you will noremlly discard the old reference if a new IndirectObject is returned.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.IndirectObject.GetHashCode
member.summary: A hash code for the IndirectObject.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.IndirectObject.GetHashCode(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.ComparisonType)
member.summary: A hash code derived from this IndirectObject. The hash code can be made up of a variety of parts of the indirect object combined together. The ID and the Atom hash codes are derived from the value of the ID and Atom respectively. The Data hash code is made from a sample of the compressed data contained in the stream. For this reason two StreamObjects, compressed differently, will return different hash codes even if the uncompressed data is identical. The data sample is kept small - in the order of a few hundred bytes - to ensure a fast response even for very large streams.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Page.StampFormXObjects(System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Removes all FormXObjects from the page by embedding them into the content.
Most Form XObjects can be embedded in the page with no difference in page appearance. However Form XObjects such as transparency groups contain structures which cannot be represented any other way. These structures are uncommon in most documents but they do occur.
In this situation you need to decide whether a change in page appearance is acceptable and that the objects should be forcably embedded. The alternative is to skip these objects and embed only those that will not affect the page appearance.
member.param: Whether to stamp FormXObjects that may cause a change in the page appearance.
member.returns: The number of FormXObjects removed from the page.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Page.GetBitmap(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Layer[])
member.summary: Render one or more layers on the current page.

remarks.para: This function renders a set of layers and returns the result as a System.Drawing.Bitmap. The Bitmap covers the smallest possible area which encompasses all the layers provided.
If this Page is not in a Doc then an exception will be raised. The function will return null if the layers argument is null or empty or the output Bitmap would be smaller than one pixel in area.

Rendering options such as resolution in DPI,are taken directly from the current XRendering settings for the doc. However automatic page rotation (XRendering.AutoRotate) is disabled so that a Layer can be rendered and then re-inserted into the page as a raster copy of itself.

Note that a layer can exist on multiple pages and indeed can be rendered in the context of a page that does not contain it. However layers typically contain references to named resources which are only available in the context of a specific page. So rendering a layer in the context of a page which does not normally contain it is prone to error unless the page and layer have been specifically consructed to allow this.

member.param: The layers to be rendered.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Page.MediaBox
member.summary: The MediaBox for the page.

remarks.para: The MediaBox defines the boundaries of the physical medium on which the page may be displayed or printed. This may include bleed areas or printing marks and also parts of the medium on which printing cannot take place because of physicsal limitations of the output technology. Any PDF drawing outside the MediaBox can be safely ignored.
These boundaries may be defined directly on the Page object or they may be inherited from a parent Pages object.
A MediaBox is mandatory for all pages so this property should never be null.

Assigning a new value to this property will change the property for the current Page rather than any Pages object from which the value may have been inherited. In this way the property exhibits a copy-on-write behavior.
Attempting to assign a null value to this property will result in a NullReferenceException being thrown.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Page.CropBox
member.summary:
The CropBox for the page.
The CropBox defines the visible part of the physical medium on which the page may be displayed or printed. This is what you see as the boundary of the page when you view a document using Acrobat Reader.
These boundaries may be defined directly on the Page object or they may be inherited from a parent Pages object.
The CropBox is optional and if this property is null it is implicitly assumed to be the same as the MediaBox.
Assigning a new value to this property will change the property for the current Page rather than any Pages object from which the value may have been inherited. In this way the property exhibits a copy-on-write behavior.
Attempting to assign a null value to this property will result in a NullReferenceException being thrown. If you want to assign an effective value of null to this property you should assign it the value of the MediaBox.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Page.TrimBox
member.summary: The TrimBox for the page.

remarks.para: The TrimBox defines the intended boundaries of the page after trimming.
These boundaries are always defined directly on the Page object. If no property has been defined then this property will be null and the effective value is assumed to be that of the CropBox.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Page.ArtBox
member.summary: The ArtBox for the page.

remarks.para: The ArtBox defines the extent of meaningful content on this page.
These boundaries are always defined directly on the Page object. If no property has been defined then this property will be null and the effective value is assumed to be that of the CropBox.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.Page.BleedBox
member.summary: The BleedBox for the page.

remarks.para: The BleedBox defines the region to which the contents of the page shall be clipped when rendered in a production environment.
These boundaries are always defined directly on the Page object. If no property has been defined then this property will be null and the effective value is assumed to be that of the CropBox.

member.summary: Rotate the image clockwise.
member.param: The number of degrees clockwise that the image should be rotated. This must be a multiple of 90.

remarks.para: This function rotates the PixMap image clockwise. The rotation angle must be a multiple of 90. If an invalid number of degrees is specified then an ArgumentOutOfRangeException will be thrown.
An image may have an associated bit mask or soft (alpha) mask. If this is the case the associated mask will be transformed as well.

When a PixMap is drawn on a page it is scaled to fit into a particular location. The scaling is separate from the PixMap itself. Rotating by 90 or 270 degrees will swap the width and height of the PixMap. Because the scaling of drawn copies is separate from the PixMap itself, any previously drawn instances of the PixMap may appear to have an incorrect aspect ratio.
After this method has been called the PixMap will no longer be compressed. You may wish to compress it using the StreamObject.Compress method or similar.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.PixMap.Flip(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Flip the image horizontally or vertically.
member.param: Whether to flip the image horizontally.
Whether to flip the image vertically.

remarks.para: This function flips the image horizontally or vertically or both. Flipping both horizontally and vertically is equivalent to a 180 degree rotation.
An image may have an associated bit mask or soft (alpha) mask. If this is the case the associated mask will be transformed as well.
Flipping horizontally will mean that pixels that were on the far right of the image will be moved to the far left and pixels on the left will be moved to the right.
Flipping horizontally will mean that pixels that were on the top of the image will be moved to the bottom and pixels that were on the bottom will be moved to the top.
After this method has been called the PixMap will no longer be compressed. You may wish to compress it using the StreamObject.Compress method or similar.

member.name: M:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Operations.EffectOperation.Apply(WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.Objects.PixMap)
member.summary: Apply effect to image.
member.param: The PixMap to which the image should be applied.

remarks.para: The effect will be applied to the PixMap. Effects normally involve wholescale changes and so it may well be necessary to change the color space and depth in order to apply the effect. If the AutoRestore property is set then the PixMap will be restored to a similar color space after processing and it will be recompressed at an appropriate quality. This default is generally what is required.

However if the AutoRestore property is not set then final output may well have different characteristics such as color space and depth. In general the final image will be uncompressed eight bit RGB no matter what was supplied.

If you are relying on particular characteristics present in the original PixMap then you should convert or recolor it after the effect has been applied. Since the final image will be left uncompressed you will likely want to recompress it using an apppopriate schema.

Whether to automatically open the default document inside a PDF portfolio rather than the portfolio itself.
If you wish to see the document the way a user would see it when it opens, them this parameter should be set to true. If you wish to operate upon the set of files embedded in the portfolio then it should be set to false.

members.member: The kerning of type. The default kerning is based on the glyph indexes and the kerning table which applies to them. This is sometimes known as format zero. There are other other types of kerning based on classes of glyphs and the relationship between ther classes. This is sometimes known as format two. In theory the two formats will produce the same result. However this depends on the accuracy with which the fonts are constructed. There are no formats one or three. As well as the standard kerning there are other forms which allow shifts perpendicular to the text flow. However this is unusual and little used and is not currently supported.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.XTextStyle.CharUsage
member.summary: The usage of characters.

member.name: P:WebSupergoo.ABCpdf10.XTextStyle.LeftMargin
member.summary: The paragraph indent (points).

members.member: The default text direction. Most Western languages have a default reading direction of left-to-right. However some other languages, notably Hebrew and Arabic, read right-to left. To further complicate matters it is quite common for languages like Hebrew to read bi-directionally - to have sections which are read left-to-right against the normal flow of text. The most common case in which this occurs is the use of numbers in text. Numbers are always read left-to-right. However it is also quite common to quote English names and again these are read in the standard English direction. This property allows you to set the default or predominant direction to be assumed for text.
